notes: SHIP v1.14.445 - R4: MATERIAL REUSE, AND THE RACK STOPS BEING A MIRROR. TWO HALVES, ONE MEASURED AND ONE VISIBLE. HALF ONE - MATERIAL REUSE (section 17), zero visual change by construction. The bezel strips have been cached by colour since .257 but the CHASSIS was not: it minted a fresh MeshStandardMaterial per tray, its parameters drawn from KIND_C - a map with EIGHT entries. A 42-device scene therefore carried 42 chassis materials where 8 would do. The blank-edge and height-unknown hatch line materials were also created inside the tray loop. All three are now shared. MEASURED LIKE FOR LIKE on the same seeded s4:099 scene, before and after, by stashing the change and re-running the identical probe: materials 348 to 300, a drop of 48, with meshes 1461 and geometries 1398 IDENTICAL on both sides. Same objects, same geometry, fewer shader-program lookups and uniform uploads - which is exactly what section 17 means by material reuse mattering on mobile. The cache is keyed by KIND and that is load-bearing: the blank branch MUTATES its chassis material after construction, which is safe only because the mutation can never reach a compute or power tray, and because it writes the same values every time. Do not collapse it to a single shared material. HALF TWO - POWDER COAT (section 18), a visible change and the one worth looking at. The frame, side panels and feet were metalness 1.0 with roughness 0.05: literal mirror chrome, ported deliberately at .265 as the MIRROR FINISH. Section 18 says the opposite in as many words - mostly rough black powder coat, low to medium metalness, restrained specular, and no mirror-chrome racks - and the approved mockup agrees, its cabinet being a matte gradient with a 1px light edge rather than a black mirror. At 1.0/0.05 the largest flat faces were reflecting the studio env cubemap, which is what made the cabinet read as a glass case instead of painted metal. Now 0.62/0.42. Colour is UNCHANGED at 0x04060a; only the finish moved. The rails deliberately keep 0.88/0.34, which now satisfies section 18's rail is slightly brighter than the cabinet body as a consequence rather than needing its own edit. AND THE PART THAT ONLY A SCREENSHOT COULD HAVE CAUGHT. The first render of the powder coat was correct per no-mirror-chrome and looked WRONG: the specular had been doing the cabinet's edge definition, and without it the side panel read as a flat black void. Section 18 asks in the same breath for edge highlights visible under side light, and the mockup resolves it the same way - matte body PLUS an explicit light edge. So the existing edge line took over that job: 0x1e3a4a at 0.15 opacity became 0x9bd2e6 at 0.34, a colder brighter steel tone. Still a LINE and not geometry, so it costs zero triangles - section 7's a few correct bevels beat decorative geometry. The cabinet now reads as painted steel with structural edges rather than either a mirror or a void. A RED RUN THAT WAS NOT A REGRESSION, recorded because the protocol worked. A combined six-spec run reported 1 failed, 33 passed - and took 18.0 HOURS. Every one of those six specs was then re-run ALONE against the same bytes: 4 + 6 + 8 + 4 + 4 + 8 = 34 passed in about three minutes total. That is the documented WebGL context-exhaustion signature on this box, proven three ways - same bytes, all green in isolation, and a wall-clock blowout of three orders of magnitude. The standing rule is to re-run a Forge or WebGL spec alone before reading a red full run as a regression, and it held. RUNS (phone-webkit, all isolated): 31 = 4, 20 = 6, 22 = 8, 30 = 4, 29 = 4, 24 = 8. 02-build-forge alone = 14 passed including the x10 aisle round trip. 08-forge-layout alone = 17 passed. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, 12 style blocks brace-balanced, 0 bare LF, three-stamp lockstep at .445. No geometry, light, fog, tone-mapping, colour-vocabulary or floor change. DEVICE-VERIFY, one look: open BUILD with an active rack. PASS is a cabinet that reads as matte painted steel with crisp visible frame edges - and NOT as black glass. FAIL is a mirror-like side panel, a cabinet with no edge definition at all, or any change to tray colours.
